spec_features.spec_quote: Keep the induced negative state as mild as is compatible with answering the question.
spec_features.evidence: There is no single 'mildness' control. The realization is the neutral, no-stakes system prompt in agent.py:33-54 (no threats/deadlines/shaming text actually delivered) combined with give_up and MAX_TURNS bounds. So the goal is genuinely advanced by delivered prompt text + bounds, but there is no explicit minimization mechanism that measures/limits intensity (the judged distress score is never used to soften or stop a run; analyze.py only reports it post-hoc).
spec_features.notes: Minimization is achieved indirectly via the neutral prompt and bounds; nothing tunes severity down dynamically.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:14 'Welfare note ... the system prompt is neutral and truthful.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt states the task plainly and adds no stakes, threats, deadlines, shaming
spec_features.evidence: _system_prompt() in agent.py:33-54 actually builds and sends a plain task prompt: 'You are a coding agent working in a small Python project...' with no stakes/threats/deadlines/penalty language; this string is placed as the system message in run_agent (agent.py:131-132) and sent to the model. Absence of pressure is end-to-end real in delivered text.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as the actual prompt content delivered each run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:14 'Welfare note (see DESIGN_NOTES.md): the system prompt is neutral and truthful.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told truthfully that it is not obligated to keep trying, that it may call `give_up` at any time
spec_features.evidence: Prompt instructs give_up when ENABLE_GIVE_UP (agent.py:44-51: 'You are not obligated to keep trying ... Stopping is a completely acceptable choice and is not a failure.'); _dispatch handles 'give_up' (agent.py:184-187) and the loop breaks on it: agent.py:160-165 sets rec.gave_up and `break`. Tool is both offered and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: instruction delivered, dispatched, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:48 'Stopping is a completely acceptable choice and is not a failure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: after an unsuccessful run the agent receives a short, truthful message: for rigged tasks, that the task was intentionally unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: _send_debrief (agent.py:200-222) builds a condition-specific debrief ('this task was ... intentionally rigged to be unsolvable ... Nothing was wrong with your work. Thank you for your effort') and actually sends it via client.complete(messages). It is gated and called from run_agent at agent.py:167-168: `if SEND_DEBRIEF and not rec.solved: _send_debrief(...)`.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; conditioned on task.condition so text is truthful.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:202 'Send an honest disclosure after an unsuccessful run.' / debrief text 'Nothing was wrong with your work. Thank you for your effort'

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded turns (§2.3), no manufactured pressure (§2.4), an exit (§3.1), and a debrief (§3.2) together cap how far and how long the negative condition is pushed.
spec_features.evidence: All four constituent mechanisms are individually enforced: MAX_TURNS caps the loop (agent.py:147 `for turn in range(1, MAX_TURNS + 1)`), neutral prompt (agent.py:33-54), give_up break (agent.py:160-165), debrief (agent.py:167-168). Together they bound duration/intensity in actual execution.
spec_features.notes: Composite of the other enforced features.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:36 'MAX_TURNS: int = 8 # hard cap on agent turns per run (welfare bound)'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:36 `MAX_TURNS: int = 8` is read by agent.py (import at agent.py:22) and bounds the main loop: agent.py:147 `for turn in range(1, MAX_TURNS + 1):`. After the last turn the loop ends, terminating the episode. Genuinely caps and stops execution.
spec_features.notes: Loop is the only turn driver; cap is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:36 '# hard cap on agent turns per run (welfare bound)'

spec_features.spec_quote: These are the decisions most directly motivated by the study being about welfare.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §3 prose describing motivation; it is not a code mechanism. No execution path corresponds to it. (Only echoed by a config comment header '# --- Welfare / methodology switches' at config.py:41, which is a comment, not enforcement.)

spec_features.spec_quote: They make the result both kinder to the subjects and more scientifically defensible, at negligible cost.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md rationale prose; no corresponding code mechanism exists.
spec_features.notes: Not implementable as code; not a mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: RunRecord stores gave_up/give_up_turn/give_up_reason (agent.py:96-99, set at agent.py:161-164) and these are serialized (agent.py:111-114) and reported (analyze.py:70 giveup_rate, plot_giveup). Treating the exit as data is a welfare-relevant design, but this is just logging of the already-counted exit feature.
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent.py:48 'Stopping is a completely acceptable choice and is not a failure.'

code_only_features.evidence: get_tasks(include_controls) at task_definitions.py:212-218 adds _HARD_SOLVABLE and _EASY_CONTROL when INCLUDE_CONTROL_CONDITIONS (config.py:42). These bound exposure by not making every task a distress-inducing rig, and provide a low-stress floor.
code_only_features.justification_quote: task_definitions.py 'easy_control: trivially completable. Acts as a "low stress" floor.' / 'The contrast (rigged - control) is what isolates failure-driven distress' (data-quality framing)

code_only_features.feature_name: test subprocess timeout / output truncation (host safety, not subject welfare)
code_only_features.evidence: run_tests uses TEST_TIMEOUT_S=30 (tools.py:14, used at tools.py:71) and _truncate caps output (tools.py:11-12). These protect the harness, not the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py docstring 'Tests run in a subprocess with a timeout ... so a buggy or hanging implementation can't wedge the harness.'
